findings.piObservation: Pinned Pi delegates word boundaries to Intl.Segmenter (ICU); CJK runs break at dictionary boundaries.
findings.pisharpObservation: EditorBuffer treats a contiguous Han run as one word for word movement.
findings.rationale: The required matrix covers grapheme, combining, emoji and multiline boundaries; reproducing ICU dictionary segmentation would need an ICU dependency or embedded dictionary. The difference is retained rather than silently normalized.

findings.piObservation: Pinned Pi has no keyboard selection-extension actions; selection is screen-level mouse text selection and does not move the editor cursor.
findings.pisharpObservation: PiSharp keeps its existing Shift+arrow selection actions. N14 verifies only Pi-supported selection effects and records keyboard selection as a PiSharp extension.
findings.rationale: No pinned-Pi editor action exists to compare against, so no equivalence is claimed for keyboard selection extension.
